cards.question: The US Open is played on which type of court?
cards.answerExplanation: The US Open is a hard-court Grand Slam in New York. Roland-Garros is the clay-court major, while Wimbledon is played on grass. Court surface affects bounce, speed, and how players build points.

cards.question: Glinda and Elphaba’s story is set in which fictional land?
cards.answerExplanation: Glinda and Elphaba are central characters in Wicked, set in the land of Oz. Narnia belongs to C. S. Lewis, Neverland to Peter Pan, and Middle-earth to The Lord of the Rings. The setting connects Wicked to the wider Wizard of Oz world.

cards.question: Greenland governs many local matters but remains part of which realm?
cards.answerExplanation: Greenland has extensive self-government but remains part of the Realm of Denmark. Canada is Greenland’s nearest large neighbor, which makes it a tempting distractor; Iceland and Norway are Nordic countries but do not include Greenland. This explains Denmark’s Arctic role.
cards.whyNow: An Arctic forum makes the political geography behind Greenland’s place in the region timely.

cards.question: To prevent a blackout, what must grid operators continually match?
cards.answerExplanation: Grid stability depends on matching electricity supply to demand in real time. Voltage also needs management, but it is not the central balance described here. If supply and demand diverge too far, outages can cascade.
cards.whyNow: Accounts of prolonged power cuts make the hidden balancing act behind a working grid relevant.

cards.question: Which process best explains new wildfire ignitions far ahead of the main flame front?
choices: Wind carries burning embers onto dry fuel
Radiant heat crosses miles and ignites fuel without contact
Smoke dries vegetation until it ignites by itself
Flames travel through ordinary soil and emerge miles ahead
cards.canonicalAnswer: Wind carries burning embers onto dry fuel
cards.answerExplanation: Wind can carry burning embers well ahead of a wildfire’s main flames, where they ignite dry, receptive fuel as spot fires. Radiant heat is mainly a near-front hazard, smoke does not make plants ignite by themselves, and surface flames do not ordinarily travel miles through mineral soil. This is how fires can jump roads, rivers, and apparent barriers.
cards.whyNow: The wildfire season discussion makes one of the most surprising ways fires spread especially relevant.
